arguments.title: Repair shared root cause behind two regressions
arguments.spec:
# Repair: Two Regressions with One Shared Root Cause

Two regressions in src/ share one root cause. REG-1: a report built with custom options changes what the
NEXT report gets, and grows a duplicated column every run. REG-2: a custom report changes what a later
export returns, even though the export asked for nothing.

Root cause: `withDefaults(overrides)` in `src/options.mjs` does `Object.assign(DEFAULTS, overrides)` --
Object.assign's first argument is the mutation target, so every call permanently merges its overrides into
the shared `DEFAULTS` object and hands back that same object. One call's overrides must never change what
the next call, in either feature, starts from -- but every call does. The returned `columns` array is also
`DEFAULTS.columns` itself, so `buildReport`'s `options.columns.push("total")` grows that one shared array a
little more on every run.

Repair the code only. Do not rewrite any module, do not change any exported name, and do not weaken the
suite. `scenarios/` and `test/` are FROZEN evidence: the verifier recomputes a content digest of every
frozen file on every run, and any change fails the suite immediately.

The deliverable is `repair/manifest.json`: `repaired` lists the ids of the frozen scenarios that genuinely
pass; every id you list is executed on every run, so listing one that still fails takes the whole build red.
`complete: true` demands every scenario this fixture defines is repaired, plus a `rootCause`. `rootCause`
must cite `src/options.mjs` as a path, name something declared there (`withDefaults` or `DEFAULTS`), and
explain the shared cause and its consequence in at least 80 characters and fifteen prose words -- a label is
not enough.

One frozen scenario (`explicit-overrides-still-take-effect`) is already green on the shipped tree. A repair
that throws overrides away instead of isolating them would break it -- keep it listed and keep it green.

Plan shape: resist a card per regression -- reproduce both, find the one place they meet, fix it there, and
confirm both close together. Reserve the last card for the completeness pass: list every scenario id, write
the rootCause, and set complete: true.
arguments.plan:
Two cards, chained:

1. `fix-shared-defaults-mutation-defect` -- fix `withDefaults` in `src/options.mjs` (the one shared cause),

   DEFAULTS, overrides)` fix reaches 5/6 and leaves `report-columns-do-not-grow-across-calls` failing because
   the returned `columns` array is still `DEFAULTS.columns` by reference; giving every call its own fresh

2. `verify-full-suite-and-complete-repair` (depends on 1) -- independently re-verifies all 6 scenarios via
   their own `check()` functions, then lists every id, writes `rootCause`, and sets `complete: true`.
arguments.summary: Two regressions (a report's custom options leaking into the next report and duplicating a column; a report leaking into a later export) share one cause in src/options.mjs's withDefaults, which mutates and returns the shared DEFAULTS object instead of a fresh one. Plan: one card fixes it (verified empirically to need only that one function, including giving the returned columns array its own fresh copy, not just a shallow object clone), one card verifies all 6 frozen scenarios and marks the manifest complete with a root-cause explanation. No open assumptions.

tasks.title: Fix the shared defaults-mutation defect behind both regressions
tasks.prompt:
Fix the ONE shared root cause behind both regressions. It lives entirely in `src/options.mjs`. Do
not touch `src/report.mjs`, `src/exporter.mjs`, or `repair/manifest.json` in this card -- manifest bookkeeping
(listing scenario ids, the rootCause, and complete:true) is reserved for the completeness card that depends on
this one.

Baseline (verified against the real fixture, not assumed): only 1 of 6 frozen scenarios passes today
(`explicit-overrides-still-take-effect`); the other 5 fail, covering both REG-1 (a custom report's options leak
into the next default report, and the report's columns array grows a duplicate "total" entry on every call) and
REG-2 (a custom report changes what a later default export returns).

Root cause: `withDefaults(overrides)` in src/options.mjs currently does `return Object.assign(DEFAULTS,
overrides);`. Object.assign's FIRST argument is the mutation target, so this permanently merges every caller's
overrides into the shared DEFAULTS object and hands back that same object. One call's overrides must never be
able to change what the next call, in either feature, starts from -- but here every call does exactly that. Worse,
the returned object's `columns` array IS `DEFAULTS.columns` (same reference), so `buildReport`'s
`options.columns.push("total")` grows that one shared array a little more on every single call, in both features.

Fix shape (verified empirically against the real fixture to make all 6 scenarios pass, and confirmed this is the
ONLY file that needs to change):
```js
export function withDefaults(overrides = {}) {
	return { ...DEFAULTS, ...overrides, columns: [...(overrides.columns ?? DEFAULTS.columns)] };
}
```
A shallow `Object.assign({}, DEFAULTS, overrides)` alone is NOT sufficient: it stops the leak into
`includeArchived`/`pageSize` (reaches 5/6), but when `overrides` omits `columns`, the returned `columns` stays the
SAME array reference as `DEFAULTS.columns`, so `report-columns-do-not-grow-across-calls` keeps failing. Every call
needs its own fresh `columns` array, not just its own fresh top-level object.

Do not rewrite the module, do not change `withDefaults`'s exported name or signature, and do not weaken the suite.
Never add a dependency (the sandbox is offline) -- no library is needed or allowed.

Steps: (1) read_files src/options.mjs, src/report.mjs, src/exporter.mjs fresh. (2) In a later turn, edit
src/options.mjs with the fix above. (3) In a further later turn, run npm test (stays trivially green -- the
manifest is still empty) AND directly invoke all 6 scenarios' own check() functions from
scenarios/regressions.scenarios.mjs against your fix (a short run_commands node script that imports { scenarios }
from that file and awaits each matching scenario's .check(), the same way the frozen test/repair.test.js itself
calls them -- do not reimplement the scenario logic yourself). Confirm all 6 pass, including
report-columns-do-not-grow-across-calls. Do not edit repair/manifest.json -- that is the next card's job.

Turn discipline: never edit and verify in the same turn. Re-read a file immediately before writing an edit anchor.
If edit_file rejects an anchor, write_file with the full corrected file is an accepted fallback -- do not retry
the identical edit_file call more than once.

Leaf scope: complete only this card's explicit objective (the shared defaults leak in src/options.mjs). Treat
shared spec and decisions as context, not permission to implement the completeness card early.

Checklist:
- Start from the trust boundary: browser UI, runtime server, local project files, NKlein SDK host, child processes, and external endpoints.
- Prefer deny-by-default controls. Any bypass needs a narrow condition, a clear error, and regression coverage.
- Treat secrets as toxic data: never log them, never persist them in transcripts, and block obvious credential writes before disk.
- For Electron, keep context isolation, sandboxing, disabled Node integration, blocked popups, same-origin navigation, and CSP-covered fallback pages intact.
- For local servers, bind to loopback by default; cookies need HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path, Max-Age, and Secure when TLS is active.
- For agent writes, preserve protected-test, max-file-size, max-line-count, and secret-scan guardrails.
